anarchist

AN-er-kist -- stress on the first syllable; the 'ch' sounds like 'k'. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Anarchist is a person who believes laws, government, and imposed order should be abolished.

The pamphlet, written by a nineteenth-century anarchist, argued that people could govern themselves without any state at all.

Example

In the history reading, one thinker -- an anarchist -- argues that every law, court, and ruler should be dismantled so that communities can organize themselves freely.

Someone whose ambition is to abolish government and imposed order entirely -- not merely to change one law or leader -- is an anarchist. The word names a specific political position, not just anyone who causes trouble.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

radical: A radical pushes for extreme, sweeping political or social change, arguing and organizing for it, but usually still within some vision of government. An anarchist goes further in one particular direction: the conviction that government and imposed order should not exist at all.

insurrectionist: An insurrectionist is actively rising up, arms in hand, to overthrow a government right now. An anarchist holds a position — that laws, rulers, and imposed order should be abolished — and may argue it entirely in print without ever joining an uprising.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

loyalist: one who supports the established government

traditionalist: one who favors keeping established customs and institutions

Where it sits · how totally authority is rejected

rebel → anarchist → nihilist

rebel vs. anarchist: Rebel is much broader and milder than anarchist -- a rebel resists some particular authority, while an anarchist opposes the very existence of government and imposed order.

nihilist vs. anarchist: A nihilist rejects even more than an anarchist: an anarchist opposes government and imposed order but may still believe in community and cooperation, while a nihilist dismisses all institutions, values, and meaning as worthless.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — an-: without (Greek)

root — arch-: ruler, leader (Greek archos)

suffix — -ist: one who believes in or practices (Greek -istes)

Put it together: Anarchist assembles neatly from Greek parts: an- ('without') plus archos ('ruler') plus -ist ('one who believes in'). An anarchist is literally 'one who believes in being without a ruler' -- a person whose goal is a society with no government at all.

Use the root in a new word: monarch: Crowds lined the avenue for hours to watch the monarch's carriage pass.

Root Check

Word Choice

Anarchist is a precise political and historical term for someone who wants to abolish government and imposed order -- not loose slang for any troublemaker. In essays and history readings, use it only when the person's actual position is opposition to the state itself.
